stemBlocks.value: The vectors a and b are equal, where a has components (2x + 1) and (y + 4), and b has components 7 and 10. (a) Determine the value of x. (b) Determine the value of y.
Think first: Equal vectors must match component by component, which splits one vector equation into two ordinary equations.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p179-q03 from workbook page 179.

contentBlocks.value: Both the horizontal and the vertical components must match

strategyBlocks.value: Equate the top components to find x and the bottom components to find y.

whyThisWorks.value: A vector carries two independent pieces of information, one for each direction, and neither can compensate for the other. So two vectors are equal only when both components agree, and a single vector equation is really a pair of separate equations — here one in x and one in y.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding the components and setting one combined equation, which loses the independence of the two.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding the components and setting one combined equation, which loses the independence of the two.

commonErrors.misconception: Matching the top of a with the bottom of b.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Matching the top of a with the bottom of b.

examTip.value: Write the two component equations on separate lines before solving — it makes the structure obvious and prevents cross-matching.

promptBlocks.value: If the vector with components (3x − 2) and 5 equals the vector with components 10 and y, find x and y.
